n: On January 21, 1836, in the nearly finished Kirtland Temple, Joseph Smith saw a vision of the celestial kingdom. Like Paul, he could not tell if he was in the body or out of it. The vision was added to the scriptures in 1976.

f.w: whether in the body or out I cannot tell

n: He saw the breathtaking gate into the kingdom, like circling flames of fire.
He saw God’s blazing throne with the Father and the Son seated on it.
The streets seemed paved with gold.
He saw Adam and Abraham—and his own parents and his brother Alvin, who had died in 1823. His parents were still alive at the time, so this was a vision of the future.

f.g: Joseph Smith Sr. and Lucy Mack Smith were living in 1836; the vision showed their future state.
Joseph’s beloved oldest brother died in November 1823 at age 25.

n: Joseph wondered how Alvin could be there, since he had died before the Restoration and was never baptized. A local minister had suggested at Alvin’s funeral that he was lost.
The Lord explains: everyone who died without knowing the gospel but would have accepted it will inherit the celestial kingdom. This opened the way for baptisms for the dead.

f.w: would have received it if they had been permitted to tarry

n: This applies also to all who will die in the future without the chance to hear it, if they would have received it wholeheartedly.
God judges by works and by the desires of the heart—a merciful principle.

f.w: according to the desire of their hearts

n: All children who die before the age of accountability (eight) are saved in the celestial kingdom.
